Notation and assumptions
as in Lemma <REF_0001>.
If the site <MATH_0001> has a final object and fibre products
then the functor <MATH_0002> satisfies
all the assumptions of Proposition <REF_0002>.
Namely, in addition to the properties mentioned in the lemma <MATH_0003>
also transforms the final object of <MATH_0004> into the final
object of <MATH_0005>. This is clear from the construction of <MATH_0006>.
Hence, if we first apply
Lemmas <REF_0003>
to <MATH_0007>
and then
Lemma <REF_0004>
to the resulting morphism of topoi
<MATH_0008>
we obtain the following statement:
Any morphism of topoi
<MATH_0009>
fits into a commutative diagram
<MATH_0010>
where the following properties hold:
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> the morphisms <MATH_0011> and <MATH_0012> are equivalences given by
special cocontinuous functors <MATH_0013> and
<MATH_0014>,
<STRUCT_0003> the sites <MATH_0015> and <MATH_0016> have fibre products, final
objects and have subcanonical topologies,
<STRUCT_0004> the morphism <MATH_0017> comes from a
morphism of sites corresponding to a functor
<MATH_0018> to which
Proposition <REF_0005>
applies, and
<STRUCT_0005> given any set of sheaves <MATH_0019> (resp.<SPACE_0001><MATH_0020>)
on <MATH_0021> (resp.<SPACE_0002><MATH_0022>) we may assume each of these is
a representable sheaf on <MATH_0023> (resp.<SPACE_0003><MATH_0024>).
<STRUCT_0006>
It is often useful to replace <MATH_0025> and <MATH_0026> by
<MATH_0027> and <MATH_0028>.

Notation and assumptions
as in Lemma <REF_0001>.
Suppose that in addition the original morphism of topoi
<MATH_0001> is an equivalence.
Then the construction in the proof of
Lemma <REF_0002>
gives two functors
<MATH_0002>
which are both special cocontinuous functors.
Hence in this case we can actually
factor the morphism of topoi as a composition
<MATH_0003>
as in Remark <REF_0003>, but
with the middle morphism an identity.
